argument: I support keeping the named catalogue as colour on the grounds of what richness actually costs to deliver in this book. Development richness is bought with 32 DP by level 10, and every DP is spent on a card or a Discipline rank, so the catalogue is not a development axis at all: it has no price, no rank and no upgrade path, and the system states that a kit adds no numbers. Moving weapon identity into the catalogue therefore adds zero DP decisions while adding 41 card re-keys and 5 tables that need a column. The cheap richness lever is already built and is one table wide: the kit's four lines, 12 priced options, 5 of them Armament, where the interesting cases are the two-tag option that pairs a one-handed weapon with a shield and the point-cost asymmetry between a ranged weapon and two-handed weapon. That is a single 13-row table carrying a real trade-off, against a 17-row catalogue duplicated at 2 locations that carries none. Deepening t-01 by the kit route is one table edit plus one glossary entry. Deepening it by the catalogue route is 3 lookups, 5 tables and 41 card re-keys, on a reprint that has already drifted in 14 of its 17 rows, so the same argument is stronger by roughly an order of magnitude in edit surface.
